entry.title: Why Your .env File Is Lying to You
entry.summary:
Two weeks ago I deployed a service that crashed on the first request. Not because the code was wrong — because process.env.DATABASE_URL was undefined and nobody caught it until a user hit the endpoint. I've made this mistake enough times to recognize the pattern: environment variables in Node.js are string | undefined. TypeScript shrugs. Validation is your problem. entry.title: Why your reCAPTCHA v3 score is low — and how to actually raise it
entry.summary:
Why your reCAPTCHA v3 score is low — and how to actually raise it
reCAPTCHA v3 is the one that never shows a checkbox or a puzzle. Instead it watches the whole session and hands the site a score from 0.0 to 1.0 — roughly "how human does this look." The site then decides what to do with it (allow, step up, block) based on its own threshold. So when your automation "fails reCAPTCHA v3," there's nothing to click — you're just scoring too low. The fix is understanding what it scores. v3 doesn't test whether you can solve something. It builds a risk score from signals across the page load and session: IP reputation — datacenter ranges score low almost by default; residential/mobile score higher.
